sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface detection of the membrane-anchored receptor confirmed by VSV-G immunostaining (L2). The construct was used in a FRET/FlAsH conformational study; ligand-binding or signalling function of the VSV-G-tagged receptor was NOT MEASURED independently of the multiply-tagged construct.
sites.rationale: HTR1B has no signal peptide; its N-terminus (residues 1–49) is extracellular by topology. L3 describes the construct architecture as [mGluR5 leader]–[VSV-G]–[5-HT1B], placing the VSV-G immediately upstream of HTR1B M1 (insert_after_residue = 0). Because no HTR1B residue number is stated, the position is topology-derived: the extracellular N-terminus is the sole terminus on the cell surface, leaving exactly one valid junction. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 390 = S (intracellular), so the prepend is the only extracellular terminal option. Full-length human 5-HT1B receptor expressed in mammalian cells with an exogenous mGluR5 leader sequence followed by the VSV-G peptide epitope prepended to the native N-terminus (residue M1); the construct also carried FlAsH in ICL3 and CFP at the C-tail. L2 explicitly states the VSV-G enables surface detection of the membrane-anchored receptor. No specific HTR1B residue number is named for the junction — the tag sits between the mGluR5 leader and HTR1B M1, making this a topology-derived prepend.

sources.claim: In addition, it contained the VSV-G peptide epitope within the extracellular N-terminal domain ( Figure 3B ).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines derive from a single publication (PMC8450432) describing one multiply-tagged full-length 5-HT1B construct. L2 and L3 ground the N-terminal VSV-G surface site; L1, L4 ground the intracellular FlAsH (ICL3) and CFP (C-tail) insertions, which are recorded in other_positions. L5 confirms the construct vector but adds no positional information. No ledger line supports a tag in ECL1 (110–123), ECL2 (187–206), or ECL3 (340–348); those loops are not proposed. The mGluR5 leader in the published construct functions as an exogenous signal peptide to drive surface trafficking; the VSV-G sits between that leader and HTR1B M1, consistent with insert_after_residue = 0.

literature_other_positions.note: FlAsH motif FLNCCPGCCMEP inserted into ICL3 (linking TM5–TM6, topology residues 230–314); intracellular loop, not a surface tag site.
CFP fused in-frame to the C-terminal tail of full-length 5-HT1B; the C-terminus (residues 372–390) is intracellular, so this is not a surface tag site.
